cr_dare_shoplift.text: Your friends dare you to steal a bag of sweets from the corner shop. The dare is for sweets. The principle is for much more.

outcomes.clean: You walk out with the sweets and a new reputation. The sweets were stale.
outcomes.caught: The shopkeeper knows your mother. You are walked home and the sweets are confiscated.

cr_cousin_scheme.text: Your cousin has a plan. It involves a van, a warehouse and a man called Little Pete, who is not little. He needs a "reliable pair of hands".

outcomes.pay: The job goes smoothly and Little Pete pays in cash. Your cousin takes credit.
outcomes.bust: The warehouse had a night shift nobody mentioned. You are arrested between two crates.

cr_fence_offer.text: A man at a car wash offers to buy "anything with a serial number, no questions". He asks several questions about your schedule.

outcomes.easy: He pays fairly and you both pretend it never happened.
outcomes.marked: He was not a fence. He was a detective with a very good car wash cover.

cr_traffic_stop.text: Blue lights fill your mirror. The officer asks if you know why he stopped you. You have several possible answers.

outcomes.warning: He gives you a warning and a tip about your tail light.
outcomes.ticket: He is immune to charm and writes the ticket slowly.
outcomes.lost: You lose them at a roundabout and your nerves somewhere after.
outcomes.pinned: A helicopter becomes involved. Your day does not recover.

cr_cop_knock.text: Two officers knock on your door. They are "just asking questions", in the way sharks are just swimming.

outcomes.believed: They leave with notes and no evidence. You stay up all night anyway.
outcomes.caught_lying: The notes contradicted themselves. Your lie contradicted the notes.

cr_getaway_driver.text: A friend asks you to wait outside a jeweller's with the engine running. It is described as "the easiest money you will ever make". It is not described accurately.

outcomes.paid: They run out, you drive off, and your share is a bag of cash.
outcomes.pinched: The alarm was quicker than your clutch. You are the only one arrested, because the others ran.

cr_found_stash.text: Behind a loose panel in your shed you find a duffel bag. It contains cash, a ski mask and a sandwich of uncertain age.

outcomes.rich: Nobody ever comes looking. You tell yourself it's an inheritance.
outcomes.owner: The owner comes looking. He is very polite, and also hurts you a little.

cr_graffiti_crew.text: A crew of teenagers asks whether you want to paint the underpass. You can bring your own cans or inhale theirs.

outcomes.masterpiece: The wall looks great. The council paints over it within a week.
outcomes.cops: A patrol car arrives while you are doing the shading. You are fined and lectured on art history.

cr_witness_threat.text: Someone you know is due to testify against you. You could scare them out of it. They could also scare you right back.

outcomes.quiet: They suddenly remember nothing. You remember everything.
outcomes.reported: They tell the police about the visit. The visit is now evidence.

cr_snitch_offer.text: A detective offers you a deal. Give up a name and your trouble gets smaller. You have several names and one conscience.

outcomes.deal: The charges drop. Your phone does not stop ringing with threats.
outcomes.burned: The name you gave was wrong. The detective is not happy, and neither are the people you named.

cr_old_accomplice.text: An old accomplice texts you. He has "one last thing" and a very clean new haircut.

outcomes.payday: It turns out to be small, boring and profitable.
outcomes.trap: The haircut was a disguise. He is working with the police now. Your lawyer is amused.

cr_job_with_record.text: The job application asks about your criminal record. The tick box is very small. Your honesty is not.

outcomes.hired: The manager shrugs. Everyone has a past, he says, and gives you a start date.
outcomes.rejected: The email arrives within the hour. It uses the phrase "not a fit".

cr_neighbourhood_watch.text: The neighbourhood watch hold a meeting about "suspicious characters". They look at you more than is natural.

cr_pyramid_pitch.text: An old classmate invites you to a "wealth seminar". The wealth is the speaker's. The seminar is your cost.

outcomes.ok: You break even. The speaker buys a new boat.
outcomes.lost: You lose a few thousand and gain several excellent motivational quotes.
outcomes.cash: You make a quick commission and lose a few friends.
outcomes.crash: The scheme collapses. Your friends remember who invited them.

cr_protection_racket.text: Two men in matching jackets suggest the local bakery needs "protection". You suggest they could be that protection. They are impressed.

outcomes.rich: The baker pays on time. The bread is excellent.
outcomes.tipped: The baker called the police. Not the friendly kind.

cr_record_background_check.text: A landlord runs a background check on you. The report arrives first, the handshake does not.

cr_unlocked_car.text: A car sits unlocked on the street, keys in the ignition, engine running. The universe appears to be testing you.

outcomes.joyride: You return it before anyone notices. Your pulse takes longer.
outcomes.pulled: A passing officer notices the stranger driving. The stranger is you.

cr_lawyer_discount.text: A lawyer on a billboard promises "Justice at a price you can afford". The price is in a font you cannot read.

outcomes.good: He is surprisingly good. Your case gets a little lighter.

pr_first_night.text: The door shuts behind you. The cell smells of bleach and quiet disappointment. Your bunk is the one nobody else wanted.

pr_cellmate.text: Your cellmate is a quiet man named Dennis who collects breadcrumbs and speaks in prophecy. He asks what you did.

outcomes.bond: Dennis nods slowly. He has heard worse. You are now friends.
outcomes.gossip: By dinner the entire wing knows. Dennis was not as quiet as advertised.

pr_gang_recruit.text: A man with more tattoos than skin leans on your bunk. He says his group takes care of its own. It is not clear what happens to everyone else.

outcomes.safe: Nobody bothers you now. Everybody else owes someone, and it is now you.
outcomes.initiation: The initiation is a favour that should have stayed unnamed. You can still walk.

pr_guard_favor.text: A guard offers to look the other way if you carry a package to the laundry. He says it is "just laundry". Laundry has never been this heavy.

outcomes.paid: You are paid in stamps and silence.
outcomes.sting: It was a test. The guard reported you. Both of you looked very surprised.

pr_contraband_phone.text: Somebody on the block sells smuggled phones for the price of a kidney. The kidney is optional.

outcomes.call: You call your family. Everyone cries, mostly you.
outcomes.found: The phone is found in a shake-down. The guards seem pleased with themselves.

pr_yard_fight.text: A man in the yard says your face looks like a debt. Several people stop what they are doing to watch.

outcomes.win: Your punch lands. So does his reputation, in your favour.
outcomes.lose: Your punch lands somewhere in the future. The rest lands on you.

pr_riot.text: Something snaps in the dining hall. Trays fly. The alarm sounds like a trumpet that gave up.

outcomes.fine: You come out with a black eye and a story.
outcomes.died: You are on the wrong side of a door at the wrong time.
outcomes.hurt: You wake up in the infirmary. It is, ironically, the quietest place in the building.

pr_shank_threat.text: A rival hands you a note: "Meet me in the laundry room". The sentence has an ending you can guess.

outcomes.peace: He wanted to apologise. Prison is odd.
outcomes.shanked: The laundry is quiet. You do not see it coming.
outcomes.stabbed: You walk out alive and with fewer organs of your own.

pr_parole_hearing.text: A panel of three people in cardigans is going to decide your future in under fifteen minutes. They have already had their coffee.

outcomes.granted: The panel nods, then nods again. You are going home.
outcomes.denied: They decline, politely, with a tone that suggests they have done this before.

pr_model_parole.text: Your file contains the word "exemplary". The warden has asked if you would like to tell the panel yourself.

outcomes.early: The panel is persuaded. You are released on parole, a little bewildered.
outcomes.no: Procedure delays everything. You wait another year with good behaviour.

pr_visitor_spouse.text: {{name}} visits you behind the glass. You pick up the receiver and both talk at once.

outcomes.stay: {{name}} says they will. You choose to believe it.
outcomes.leave: {{name}} says they need time. The glass seems thicker afterward.

pr_visitor_mother.text: {{name}} comes to visit and brings a bag of food that security throws away. She says she is not angry. She is lying beautifully.

outcomes.yes: She slides you an envelope through the system. Her sigh stays with you.
outcomes.no: She shakes her head. It is a good lesson in motherhood.

pr_library.text: The prison library has eleven books, three of them detective novels. You fall for the irony before the plot.

pr_work_detail.text: The prison offers you a job in the kitchen or the laundry. Both pay cents an hour, in a currency of mild dignity.

pr_escape_attempt.text: A loose vent, a night shift, a plan Dennis drew on a napkin. He insists it is foolproof. He is the fool.

outcomes.out: You squeeze through, climb the wall and reach the road. You are free, in a sense that will need a lawyer.
outcomes.caught: The siren is faster than your legs. They take your shoelaces as punishment.

pr_snitch_offer.text: A guard offers you a lighter sentence for information about the contraband ring. He mentions your cellmate by first name.

outcomes.reward: Your file gets thinner. Nobody speaks to you again.
outcomes.revenge: Word gets out. The infirmary becomes your second home.

pr_food_strike.text: The meatloaf has become sentient and it is angry. The inmates organise a hunger strike. They ask you to join.

outcomes.win: The kitchen promises to improve. They add salt.
outcomes.punished: Management responds with cold sandwiches and a lecture on solidarity.

pr_solitary.text: You are sent to solitary for something that was a misunderstanding by the standards of nobody. The walls are the same colour as time.

pr_gym.text: The prison gym has a bench, a rusted barbell and a strict hierarchy. You are on the lowest rung and the bench.

outcomes.good: You hold your own. His respect is physical but real.
outcomes.bad: You learn some humility in the form of a rib.

pr_education.text: The prison offers an education programme. The teacher has a PhD and a sign-in sheet.

outcomes.pass: You graduate with a certificate nobody on the outside will understand.
outcomes.fail: The exam is invigilated by the person who stole your lunch.

pr_appeal.text: A cellmate with the confidence of a barrister reads your case file and says there is "a technicality". He pronounces it with relish.

outcomes.win: The court agrees there is a technicality. You are released.
outcomes.lose: The court agrees that you were guilty and that you wrote badly.

pr_commissary_poker.text: There is a game of poker behind the laundry. The stakes are cigarettes, favours and the dignity of your bunk.

outcomes.won: You win a month of supplies and a man's grudge.
outcomes.lost: You lose your pudding rights and a favour you hadn't yet earned.
